system_description.narrative_title: Gulf proxy war disrupts energy, shipping and aviation
system_description.narrative_summary: A sharp escalation of Iran-backed and Houthi attacks on Saudi airports, oil infrastructure and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is driving military responses, diplomatic friction and emergency policy moves while pushing oil and diesel markets into acute stress. The attacks have forced airlines to suspend routes, prompted IEA and governments to release or plan stock interventions, raised insurance and freight costs, and amplified the risk of wider regional confrontation with global economic spillovers. Markets, supply chains and national security postures are interacting as an open system where kinetic strikes, shipping disruptions and energy flows mutually reinforce volatility.
system_description.scope: Inside the system boundary: actors (Houthis, Iran, Saudi Arabia, US, UK, coalition partners), concrete assets and sites (Riyadh airports, Saudi Aramco facilities, tankers, refineries, the Strait of Hormuz), processes and variables (missile/drone strikes, maritime attacks, shipping transits, freight and insurance rates, crude and refined-fuels flows, refinery margins, diesel inventories, oil price volatility), institutional responses (military strikes, sanctions, IEA stock releases, airline cancellations) and near-term economic outcomes (energy price inflation, supply chain disruptions).
adjacent_subsystems: Global refined fuels (diesel) market and refining capacity
International aviation and commercial air travel networks
Regional Middle East security and proxy warfare dynamics
evidence_headlines: Missile strike on Riyadh airport kills 12 and injures hundreds
Ships in Hormuz strait hit by worst spate of attacks since start of war
Oil prices jump on tanker attacks and slowing flows through Strait of Hormuz
Airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks
Diesel shortages could persist well into 2027, IEA says

variables.name: Kinetic attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of missile, drone and surface-to-surface strikes against land-based infrastructure and installations.

variables.name: Maritime attack rate
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of hostile actions against commercial vessels and maritime assets at sea.

variables.name: Chokepoint transit flow
variables.description: The volume and rate of commercial vessel transits through a critical maritime chokepoint.

variables.name: Crude export flow
variables.description: The volume and rate of crude oil exports moving from production areas to international markets.

variables.name: Refined diesel flow
variables.description: The volume and rate of diesel and other refined fuel shipments available for regional and global distribution.

variables.name: Refinery utilization
variables.description: The proportion of refining capacity actively operating and processing crude into refined products.

variables.name: Refinery margin index
variables.description: The average processing margin between crude input costs and refined product prices across refiners.

variables.name: Diesel inventory level
variables.description: The total onshore and afloat stocks of diesel available in a market or region.

variables.name: Shipping freight rate
variables.description: The market price level for hiring vessels and transporting oil and goods by sea (time-charter and voyage rates).

variables.name: Marine insurance premium
variables.description: The cost level of hull, war risk and related insurance coverage for vessels operating in the region.

variables.name: Aviation route availability
variables.description: The share of scheduled air routes and services considered operational and safe for commercial flights.

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing global market price level for benchmark crude oil grades.

variables.name: Oil price volatility
variables.description: The short- to medium-term variability and uncertainty in crude oil price movements.

variables.name: Military response rate
variables.description: The frequency and scale of kinetic counter-actions and strikes undertaken by state or coalition military forces.

variables.name: Diplomatic tension level
variables.description: The intensity of interstate diplomatic hostility, sanctions pressure and formal political confrontation signals.

variables.name: Market risk premium
variables.description: The excess return demanded by market participants for bearing geopolitical and supply-risk uncertainty in energy and shipping markets.

catalysts.title: IEA emergency diesel release (20m+ barrels)
catalysts.description: Coordinated IEA release of over 20 million barrels of diesel to markets imminently to relieve tight diesel supply.
catalysts.rationale: IEA to release more than 20m barrels of diesel; IEA to speed up oil stocks release (IEA diesel release headlines).

catalysts.title: Escalating Houthi campaign against Saudi targets
catalysts.description: Houthis continue strikes on Saudi airports, Aramco and vow further attacks, implying sustained escalation of attacks on infrastructure and aviation.
catalysts.rationale: Houthis attack Riyadh airport, Aramco HQ and vow more attacks; ships hit and sink near Hormuz (multiple headlines).

catalysts.title: Continued strikes and sinkings near Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: Repeated projectiles and sinkings in the Strait of Hormuz keep transit risk high, raising freight and insurance costs and reducing flows.
catalysts.rationale: Two ships sink and multiple vessels struck near Hormuz; shipping costs spike and captains paid high premiums (Hormuz attack headlines).

catalysts.title: Risk of US/coalition direct strikes on Iran
catalysts.description: U.S. deliberations and heightened rhetoric raise the near-term risk of direct strikes on Iranian targets, potentially broadening the war.
catalysts.rationale: U.S. weighs use of 'mother of all bombs'; Iran fortifying sites and US hits tanker — risk of direct strikes rises (escalation headlines).

catalysts.title: Broader IEA coordinated oil stock release (400m+ barrels)
catalysts.description: IEA signals a larger, multi-month program to release strategic stocks (exceeding 400m barrels) to stabilize markets.
catalysts.rationale: IEA says total stock release will exceed 400m barrels and to speed up releases (IEA stock release headlines).

catalysts.title: Diesel supply squeeze persisting into 2027
catalysts.description: IEA and market warnings point to a prolonged global diesel shortage, sustaining price pressure and refining margin distortion.
catalysts.rationale: IEA warns diesel squeeze will drag into 2027; global diesel shortages and price rises expected (IEA diesel shortage headlines).

catalysts.title: Airlines cancel Saudi routes; airport closures persist
catalysts.description: Airlines and regulators suspend flights to Saudi airports and events, reducing available commercial aviation routes and services.
catalysts.rationale: FAA warns airlines; airlines cancel flights and Riyadh airport to remain shut this week (aviation disruption headlines).

catalysts.title: Postponement of EU-Gulf summit delays de-escalation
catalysts.description: Postponed diplomatic summits and delayed events reduce immediate avenues for negotiation, prolonging elevated tensions and market risk.
catalysts.rationale: EU and Gulf states postpone summit; wave of Saudi events delayed after Houthi attacks (summit postponement headlines).
